question: Is it reasonable to posit an unseen cause when an established cause is already observed?
premises: A cause may be established or yet to be established
When an observed cause is present, it accounts for the effect
Positing an unseen cause in that case is not proper
inference: An unseen supposition is unwarranted when an observed cause suffices
plain_english: When what is established is seen to be present, it is not proper to suppose an unseen cause.
